What fills this page

Every number here is a count over stored rows, so the page stays empty until something has been recorded. Three actions produce data, and any one is enough:

· Run a session. Tool activity records bounded signals — Claude Code sessions record per-tool events via hooks; Codex sessions record turn-complete and approval events.
· Teach Wanigan directly. The button above creates a cited Inbox proposal from your own words.
· Run a review gate. Gate passes and failures are recorded as signals with their citations.

Repeated observations across independent tasks are consolidated into proposals every 5 minutes while Wanigan is open.

Hook events

Fictional UI fixture; runtime capability checks are not performed.
These hooks only report what a Codex session did. They print nothing and decide nothing, so the trust gate does not cover Codex.
Accounts

Run a work login and a personal login side by side, on any agent that keeps its configuration in a directory. Each account is its own directory, and the agent keys its stored sign-in to that directory — so two sessions can be signed in as two different people at once.

A session picks its account from the launcher, then the project’s saved account, then the default. An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in Wanigan’s environment outranks every stored sign-in; the launcher says so when one is set.

Provider packs

A pack is a manifest of launch profiles. Trusted and enabled are separate: trusting a digest grants nothing, and enabling one only affects sessions started afterwards.

Re-read from disk
⚠ The pack registry answered, and it is empty — not even the built-in manifests, which ship inside the app and should always be listed. Re-read from disk; if they are still missing, this install is incomplete and no session can start.

A profile only becomes launchable when its pack is enabled and Wanigan finds the CLI it names. Installed agent runtimes above is that second half: 2 of 2 detected.

Claude Platform API key

Needed for Batches — estimating, dry runs, and submitting. Agent sessions do not use it; they authenticate through their own CLI.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in the environment and takes precedence over anything stored here.
key installed

Workspace ID — required for identity-linked keys

Console → Settings → Workspaces. Sent as the anthropic-workspace-id header on every request. Plain API keys ignore it, so leaving it set is harmless.

This is not your Claude Code subscription. The Batches API bills per token against a Claude Platform account with its own credit balance. Get a key at console.anthropic.com/settings/keys. A Claude Code OAuth token is rejected.

Key storage and workspace IDs
GLM Coding Plan

Runs GLM through the installed Claude Code runtime, with the Z.ai Coding Plan endpoint and Wanigan’s normal sessions, attachments, code review, worktrees, MCP configuration and headless runs.

WANIGAN_GLM_KEY is set in the environment and takes precedence over anything stored here — the fingerprint below is that key, and Verify reports on it. A stored key also exists; Remove clears that one, and sessions keep using the environment.
Coding Plan key installed
Verify live catalogue
Remove
Replace Z.ai key
Save & verify

The key is verified against api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/models before Wanigan saves it, then encrypted in your macOS Keychain. Wanigan does not show or log the key.

DeepSeek

Runs DeepSeek through the installed Claude Code runtime using DeepSeek’s Anthropic-compatible endpoint. It gets the same Wanigan terminal, review, policy, worktree and headless-run controls as Claude and GLM.

WANIGAN_DEEPSEEK_KEY is set in the environment and takes precedence over anything stored here — the fingerprint below is that key, and Verify reports on it. A stored key also exists; Remove clears that one, and sessions keep using the environment.
DeepSeek key installed
Verify live catalogue
Remove
Replace DeepSeek key
Save & verify

Wanigan verifies the key against api.deepseek.com/models, then stores it encrypted in your macOS Keychain. The key is never shown, logged or sent to a renderer.

Grok · xAI

Runs Grok through the installed Claude Code runtime using xAI’s Anthropic-compatible endpoint. It gets the same Wanigan terminal, review, policy, worktree and headless-run controls as Claude, GLM and DeepSeek.

WANIGAN_XAI_KEY is set in the environment and takes precedence over anything stored here — the fingerprint below is that key, and Verify reports on it. A stored key also exists; Remove clears that one, and sessions keep using the environment.
xAI key installed
Verify live catalogue
Remove
Replace xAI key
Save & verify

Wanigan verifies the key against api.x.ai/v1/models, then stores it encrypted in your macOS Keychain. This is a pay-as-you-go key from console.x.ai; a Grok Pro or SuperGrok subscription does not carry API credit, and its consumption cannot be read the way a Claude or Codex plan's can — so Grok appears under what you spend, never under what is left.
